prompt:
Image 1 is the pose and layout guide: four grey clay maquettes of this treant in a 2 by 2 grid, one action in each cell, rendered from the game's battle camera. Copy from it exactly, cell by cell, the camera angle, the direction the body faces, the pose, the figure's size and its place in the cell. Do not copy its smooth clay surfaces, its simplified round shapes or the thickness of its limbs: the body, its anatomy and every detail follow Image 2.
Image 2 is the approved painted game cutout of this exact treant, standing at rest, seen from the same camera in the same view. Paint the same individual, with exactly the same head, shapes, proportions, colours, materials, markings and equipment, in the same painting style and the same light, now in the actions of Image 1. It must be unmistakably the same treant in all four cells.

One sheet: four painted figures of the same treant, full body, one in each cell of a 2 by 2 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF) background, as game cutouts. Read left to right, top row first:
Top left: winding up a blow: rearing back, both branch arms raised high above the crown with the twig fingers spread, the trunk leaning back.
Top right: slamming down: the trunk bent forward, both branch arms brought down hard so that their twig fingers strike the ground in front of it, one root-leg stepped forward.
Bottom left: struck and recoiling: the trunk leaning back, both branch arms flung out to the sides, one root-leg stepping back, the face grimacing.
Bottom right: toppled and dead: fallen flat on its back on the ground like a felled tree, its crown toward the upper right of the image (it fell backwards, away from us), the branch arms limp and spread, the root-legs sticking up.
Every cell takes its pose from Image 1, never from Image 2: Image 2 shows only what the treant looks like, and its standing pose must not be copied into any cell. Each pose is strong and unmistakable at a glance.

Camera: high above and in front, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at a miniature on a table; orthographic, with no perspective. The treant faces toward us and to the lower left of the image, as in Image 1 and Image 2: we see its face from above, its chest and its left side. It is foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head, the shoulders or back and the upper body are large, the legs short.

Light: outdoor daylight, exactly as in Image 2; the figure stays as dark and as muted as in Image 2, lit only by small warm and cool highlights, never washed out or brightened. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows. Nothing glows more than it does in Image 2. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, exactly the hand of Image 2; a muted earthy palette with its own colours exactly as Image 2 shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette in every pose. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The creature: a Treant, the walking tree of the reference portrait, summoned by Thornwood druids (size 4, about three and a half men tall): its trunk is its body and head, two long branch arms ending in knotted twig fingers, two short stumpy legs that splay into roots; its face is in the bark near the top of the trunk. It is a treant only a century old: a thick knotted trunk of grey-green alder bark furred with moss; its face is formed in the bark, not a human face: a broad brow ridge of bark, a low rounded bulge where a nose would be, two small dark hollow knotholes for eyes, a mouth that is only a dark crooked split low in the trunk; no beard. Its marks, every one painted clearly: a low crown of short thick budding twigs with a few small pale-green leaves; curled young fern fronds growing from the moss on its shoulders; grey-green alder bark furred with moss; two small dark knothole eyes under a broad brow ridge of bark. Seen from in front and above, its bark face, knothole eyes and crown read clearly.

Size: in each cell the figure fills the cell exactly as its maquette does in Image 1 and stands in the same place, with clean background all round it; nothing is cropped and no part of one figure reaches into a neighbouring cell.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow. No pink, magenta, violet or purple anywhere on the figure.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, dividing lines between the cells, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; other creatures or people; a cropped figure; fire, flames, breath, smoke, sparks, floating embers, magic light or mist (the game draws every effect).
